summary: In this excerpt from Kate Douglas Wiggin's Rebecca of Sunnybrook Farm (labelled 'Book 11 — part 85'), Miranda and Jane rest while Rebecca prepares the brick house for expected company, which includes returned missionaries from Syria. Rebecca works quickly to tidy the two south chambers, lays fires and supplies, and the sisters approve. Miranda also decides to bake pork and beans, and Rebecca transforms the parlor with her rose-shaded lamp and rearranges the ornaments before guests such as Brother Milliken arrive.
one_line: Rebecca readies the brick house, parlor and bedrooms for returned missionaries from Syria while her aunts rest.
key_facts: Miranda tells Rebecca that Jane and she will lie down until five o'clock and that she should not let her get up 'a minute past five.'
Miranda says it is half past three when she decides to rest and cook supper.
Miranda bakes a pot of beans in the middle of the week, saying they will come in handy.
Miranda recalls that her father used to say nothing 'went right to the spot with returned missionaries like pork 'n' beans 'n' brown bread.'
Rebecca is given a free hand to prepare the house, the only time in her life she has been allowed to do so.
Rebecca fills pitchers, lays out soap and matches, and sets newspaper, kindling and wood in the boxes in the bedrooms.
Rebecca lights a large stick of wood in each air-tight stove to take the chill off the rooms, as the guests are 'right from Syria.'
Rebecca's own lamp, her second Christmas present from Mr. Aladdin, stands on a marble-topped table in the corner of the parlor.
The lamp's rose-colored shade transforms the stiff and gloomy parlor into a place 'where one could sit and love one's neighbor.'
There is a cheerful blaze in the open stove in the front parlor and a fire laid on the hearth in the back room.
Miranda asks Rebecca whether they should open the parlor, and Rebecca says they did so on Thanksgiving and Christmas.
Rebecca moves the wax flowers off the mantelpiece so they won't melt, and puts the shells, coral and green stuffed bird on top of the what-not.
Brother Milliken is coming over to see Mr. Burch about business.
